objectives.title: Record raw data in a fully ruled table with no units in the body.
objectives.syllabus_text: Record only the raw data (unprocessed results) as quantitative data and qualitative observations in a fully ruled table with no units in the body of the table

objectives.title: Head table columns with the quantity and unit, independent variable first.
objectives.syllabus_text: prepare a table with a heading for the independent variable in the left column or top row with appropriate units and a heading for the dependent variable with units

objectives.title: Record measurements to the same number of significant figures, set by the instrument.
objectives.syllabus_text: record quantitative data to the same number of significant figures dependent on the measuring instrument used

objectives.title: Show every step and the reasoning in a calculation.
objectives.syllabus_text: show calculations clearly showing all the steps in the calculation and their reasoning

objectives.title: Give calculated values to the same number of significant figures as, or one more than, the least accurate measurement.
objectives.syllabus_text: use the correct number of significant figures for calculated quantities. This should be the same number of significant figures as (or one more than) the measured quantity of least accuracy.

objectives.title: Choose between a graph and a chart, then present it clearly and accurately.
objectives.syllabus_text: select whether data should be shown as a graph or chart and then present the graph or chart clearly and accurately

objectives.title: Put the independent variable on the x-axis and the dependent variable on the y-axis, both labelled with units.
objectives.syllabus_text: axes with the independent variable on the x-axis, clearly labelled (to match the relevant table heading) with units where appropriate and the dependent variable (to match the relevant table heading) on the y-axis labelled with units, where appropriate

objectives.title: Choose scales that use most of the grid and can be read easily.
objectives.syllabus_text: a scale where both axes should use most or all of the grid available

objectives.title: Plot every point accurately as a small cross or dot in a circle.
Join plotted points correctly: line of best fit, smooth curve or ruled straight lines, without extrapolating.
objectives.syllabus_text: for a graph (based on data provided) the plotted points should be connected with a clear, sharp and unbroken

objectives.title: Draw bars separated for discrete or categorical data and joined for continuous data.
objectives.syllabus_text: bars should be separated for discrete or categorical data and joined for continuous data

performance_tasks.brief: A Paper 3 style investigation task (about 10 marks): an experiment described in words with our own readings in a table. The learner decides variables, controls and how to measure, draws up the results table (quantity and unit headings, consistent significant figures), plots or describes the graph, calculates a value with working, identifies sources of error and suggests an improvement. Readings are ours and are labelled as such.
performance_tasks.objective_ids: choose 2-4 objectives from this topic that the task genuinely exercises

performance_tasks.brief: A second Paper 3 style task (about 10 marks), different in setting from the first and fitted to this topic. Where the topic concerns microscopy, drawing or measuring specimens: a specimen or photomicrograph described in words with measurements given, asking what a plan diagram or cell drawing would show, a graticule calibration or actual-size or magnification calculation with working in micrometres, a comparison of two specimens by observable features only, and an improvement. Otherwise: a second, different investigation (a different experiment, data set or results table) testing the same skills as this topic's objectives. Values and readings are ours and are labelled as such.
performance_tasks.objective_ids: choose 2-4 objectives from this topic that the task genuinely exercises

ao_mix_note: The syllabus states its AO weights as a share of MARKS, so planned_ao_mix_by_marks is the one that answers "does this resource match the exam". It values each card at the tariff of the question it models, split across the AOs the card declares, and values each performance task at the marks of the paper part it models. The count-based mix below is reported only because it is what a reader expects to see; do not balance against it. AO shares by ITEM COUNT: Every objective needs one recall anchor, so AO1 has a structural floor of about 46% in this topic (11 objectives against 24 slots) and cannot reach the None% target by count however many other cards are added - padding the bank to chase it makes the resource worse. The framework already measures the AO4 share in practice time rather than by count for the same reason. Treat AO1 above target as expected, and AO2/AO3/AO4 below target as the thing worth fixing.
